title: Bound authentication-state retention and failed-start cleanup
verify: RED: With a fake clock, issue expired and abandoned authentication states and observe that the current Map retains expired entries; induce provider begin/configuration failure after issue and observe that the just-issued state remains retained.

GREEN: State issue and consume remove expired records as part of their bounded operation, and a provider begin failure discards the just-issued state without deleting valid sibling states; no background cleanup, capacity policy, durable store, or unrelated state lifecycle is introduced.

VERIFY: Independently run fake-clock retention, valid-sibling preservation, expired-consume, and failed-provider-start probes with deterministic state factories; compare observable reuse/consumption behavior and state snapshots before/after, then run the full project gates and safe cleanup.

evidence: Verifier-owned fake-clock and transport probe passed 1 file / 4 tests and covered full issue/consume expiry cleanup, failed-start discard, valid sibling preservation, safe 502, and unchanged account/identity/invitation/session state.
Fresh verifier-owned focused suite passed 2 files / 17 tests; check, build, and full test passed with 21 files / 81 tests.

Source scan found no background worker or persistence path and confirmed route delegation through public transport/Identity & Access/provider boundaries; executor receipts remained supporting-only and pre-implementation GREEN was accepted.
The verification record was produced before lifecycle closure; no code, W9/TASK-022 artifact, or mb-sync action changed during verification.

Independent hostile review found no material break across retention cleanup, failed-start scope, sibling preservation, product-state isolation, no-worker/no-persistence anti-goals, and architecture boundary.
Semantic evidence uses the fresh verifier-owned disposable probe, source/boundary inspection, and green native gates; no executor receipt was used as independent proof.
The semantic review was produced before lifecycle closure; no lifecycle, code, W9/TASK-022 artifact, or mb-sync action changed during review.

evidence_required: FT-001-AC-004 / REQ-002 / .memory-bank/contracts/provider-adapters.md#failure-and-ownership-rules RED: provider-start failure or expired auth state leaves a retained live capability or permits partial callback state; GREEN: failed start returns the safe provider error, expired records are removed during the bounded operation, and account/identity/invitation/session state is unchanged; decisive comparison: state-before/state-after equality and no usable failed-attempt capability; artifact: .tasks/TASK-023-T3-FT-001-W10/ and .protocols/TASK-023-T3-FT-001-W10/.

FT-001-AC-007 / REQ-001 / REQ-002 / REQ-014 / .memory-bank/contracts/authentication-transport.md#browser-bound-callback-state-and-bounded-retention RED: an expired or abandoned invitation authentication state remains retained, or failed provider start leaves a live invitation capability; GREEN: issue/consume cleanup and failed-start discard preserve valid sibling state while invitation/account/identity/session state remains unchanged; decisive comparison: expired/failed state is unusable and the invitation snapshot is equal before and after rejection; artifact: .tasks/TASK-023-T3-FT-001-W10/ and .protocols/TASK-023-T3-FT-001-W10/.
purpose: Make the existing process-local authentication-state TTL a real bounded retention rule and close the failed provider-start leak.
success_outcome: Expired authentication-state records are removed during issue/consume and a failed provider start removes only its newly issued record, while valid sibling flows remain usable and no new persistence or cleanup service exists.
anti_goals: Do not add a background cleanup worker, second persistence store, cache, global capacity policy, or process-restart recovery mechanism.
Do not broaden cleanup into invitation, session, account, or provider identity lifecycle changes.
Do not change the browser-binding contract from TASK-022, provider protocols, accepted architecture, or any W9 task/history artifact.

stop_conditions: Stop and route to /spec-design if bounded cleanup requires changing the accepted one-server modular-monolith + SQLite architecture, adding durable auth-state persistence, or introducing a background worker/event mechanism.
Stop if cleanup requires a new product retention/capacity decision, changes invitation/session/provider lifecycle semantics, or changes the provider verification contract.
Stop if any W9 task card, protocol, execution evidence, semantic evidence, lifecycle, or retry history would need modification.

constraints: Retain the accepted five-minute state TTL and process-local Map; cleanup is bounded to issue/consume and failed provider begin.
Failed provider begin must discard only the state created for that attempt and must preserve any other unexpired state capability.
Use deterministic fake-clock and disposable transport fixtures with safe rerun/cleanup; no live credentials, production database, or network dependency.
invariants: No expired auth-state record remains retained after the bounded issue/consume operation completes.
A provider-start failure leaves no newly issued auth-state record while valid unrelated states remain usable.
Cleanup does not mutate account, identity, invitation, or session state.
verification_targets: Existing FT-001 provider-failure/invitation regression / REQ-001 / REQ-002 / REQ-014: fake-clock and injected-provider transport probes observe expiry cleanup, failed-start discard, valid sibling preservation, safe provider error, and unchanged product state.
